structural-causal.name: bottleneckControl
structural-causal.basis: Power and data-center footprint can control a scarce physical input to AI compute deployment.

structural-causal.name: scenarioRobustness
structural-causal.basis: Contracted hyperscaler demand supports utilization, but concentrated customer exposure and phased execution create binary schedule risk.

structural-causal.name: substitutionResilience
structural-causal.basis: Compute demand is robust, but hyperscalers can self-build or source from competing infrastructure providers.

discovery-weak-signals.name: hyperscaler AI infrastructure demand
discovery-weak-signals.basis: A named multi-year customer contract materially strengthens evidence that IREN's power-and-data-center footprint can convert into AI cloud demand.

discovery-weak-signals.name: financialOperatingMomentum
discovery-weak-signals.basis: AI Cloud revenue expanded about eightfold year over year and operating ARR reached $1 billion, but consolidated FY26 net loss was $702.6 million and Q4 adjusted EBITDA fell amid platform investment.

discovery-weak-signals.name: bottleneckControl
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Owned power, land, data centers, compute and software plus largely sold 2026 capacity indicate control of scarce power-to-compute infrastructure.

discovery-weak-signals.name: scenarioRobustness
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Customer diversification and contracted capacity reduce single-path demand risk, while rapid AI infrastructure buildout remains capital intensive and commissioning-dependent.

discovery-weak-signals.name: catalystScore
discovery-weak-signals.basis: The gap between $1 billion operating ARR and $4 billion contracted ARR creates a measurable commissioning and customer-acceptance catalyst through year-end 2026.

discovery-weak-signals.name: crossDivisionLeverage
discovery-weak-signals.basis: The Mirantis acquisition adds orchestration, monitoring, lifecycle management and enterprise support on top of IREN's power, data-center and compute layers, creating a more integrated infrastructure stack.

discovery-weak-signals.name: supplyChainResilience
discovery-weak-signals.basis: IREN has relationships across multiple GPU/OEM vendors and multiple GPU generations, but the 10-K explicitly says GPU/networking demand exceeds supply and certain AI hardware comes from a limited supplier set.

discovery-weak-signals.name: scenarioRobustness
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Geographic pipeline diversification and multi-vendor compute broaden deployment options, while delivery still depends on power, construction, hardware availability and substantial financing.

discovery-weak-signals.name: bottleneckControl
discovery-weak-signals.basis: The disclosed multi-gigawatt site pipeline plus integrated compute/software stack gives IREN control over scarce power-to-compute conversion capacity, though execution remains required before planned MW become productive capacity.

adversarial-red-team.name: financingRisk
adversarial-red-team.basis: Large equipment and infrastructure commitments create substantial capital requirements before full revenue conversion.

adversarial-red-team.name: concentrationRisk
adversarial-red-team.basis: A very large named customer contract can make execution and renewal outcomes disproportionately important.

adversarial-red-team.name: confidenceInflation
adversarial-red-team.basis: Contract value and annualized run-rate should not be treated as present revenue or profit before commissioning.

expectations-execution.name: contract conversion
expectations-execution.basis: Large contracted demand is positive, but value realization depends on financing, procurement, construction, energization and GPU deployment occurring on schedule.

expectations-execution.name: expectationsExecution
expectations-execution.basis: Horizon 1 delivery and rapid AI revenue growth demonstrate execution, but most contracted ARR still depends on capacity becoming operational and accepted.

expectations-execution.name: expectationsExecution
expectations-execution.basis: Horizon 1 acceptance is concrete execution evidence, but remaining tranches retain delivery windows and grace periods, so future contract conversion is not yet realized.

expectations-execution.name: pricingPower
expectations-execution.basis: The filing establishes large contract value and prepayment structure but does not provide enough comparable unit economics to infer durable pricing power without Alpha's calibration.

thesisQuality.basis: Strong contracted hyperscaler demand, Horizon 1 acceptance and integrated power-to-compute footprint support a strong band; capital intensity and unproven full contract conversion cap the value below exceptional.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Rapid AI-cloud expansion and liquidity are offset by FY2026 net loss, large commitments, debt and financing dependence, supporting mixed/unproven rather than strong operating economics.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Independent market evidence shows a high enterprise value relative to trailing revenue; substantial AI optionality exists but present valuation requires meaningful future conversion, placing the factor at the low end of mixed/unproven.

catalystScore.basis: Horizon 2-4 commissioning/acceptance and conversion of contracted ARR are multiple material identifiable catalysts, with contractual windows extending into early Q2 2027.

governancePower.basis: Formal independent-board and audit/risk oversight requirements plus audited ICFR support an adequate-to-strong governance band, but limited evidence of long-duration capital-allocation outcomes prevents a higher score.

alignment2036.basis: Power, data-center and accelerated-compute infrastructure directly serve durable AI/critical digital-infrastructure demand across plausible long-duration scenarios.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Power, data centers, compute and Mirantis software/support create several reusable layers and demand channels, though economics remain dominated by infrastructure deployment.

bottleneckControl.basis: Multi-gigawatt site pipeline and integrated power-to-compute capability participate in scarce power/data-center constraints; planned MW are not assumed to be financed, energized or productive.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Geographic and vendor diversification plus customer prepayments broaden resilience, while financing, commissioning and customer concentration keep material scenario dependence.

substitutionResilience.basis: Integrated infrastructure and qualification/commissioning create friction, but hyperscaler self-build and competing GPU-cloud providers remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Multiple GPU generations and OEM/vendor relationships provide redundancy, but the 10-K explicitly identifies constrained GPU/networking supply and limited supplier sets.

pricingPower.basis: Large contract value and tranche prepayments indicate some economic leverage, but comparable unit economics and realized margins are not disclosed, so durable pricing power remains unproven.

riskEvidence.basis: High capital commitments, $7.976b principal debt, covenant/secured-financing exposure, dilution risk, constrained hardware supply and commissioning/customer concentration create material downside even with strong liquidity and prepayments.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Primary FY2026 SEC filing, issuer governance documents, independent current valuation and same-cycle Scout/Beta source-addressed assists cover all 12 components; remaining unknowns concern future realization rather than missing present evidence.

scoreRecord.thesis: IREN can convert scarce power and data-center capacity into an integrated AI-infrastructure platform with contracted hyperscaler demand, but value realization depends on disciplined financing, commissioning and margin conversion.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Capital intensity, leverage, dilution, constrained hardware supply and customer/commissioning concentration can make headline contracted demand materially less valuable than expected.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Acceptance and revenue conversion of Microsoft Horizon 2-4 tranches through contractual delivery/grace windows extending into early Q2 2027.

items.risk: The contract requires large-scale phased delivery and depends on infrastructure/GPU commissioning; contract value is not equivalent to recognized revenue or profit.
Capital intensity and customer concentration can amplify downside if commissioning slips or contracted economics differ from headline run-rate expectations.
Successor bottlenecks are capital and execution intensive and can delay conversion of contracted demand into operating capacity.
Customer concentration reduces resilience if a major contract is modified or not renewed.
Construction, energization, GPU delivery and commissioning slippage can defer revenue while capital obligations remain.
Hyperscaler self-build and competing GPU-cloud providers can pressure renewal economics over time.
The evidence base is currently concentrated in one issuer source and lacks a fresher phase-by-phase commissioning update.
Revenue conversion can lag headline contracted capacity when commissioning or acceptance is delayed while capital obligations continue.
Customer concentration links infrastructure financing resilience to a small number of counterparties and deployment outcomes.
Rapid GPU obsolescence and limited supplier availability can raise replacement capital needs or weaken utilization economics.
Contracted ARR is an operating metric rather than GAAP revenue and remains subject to commissioning, testing and customer acceptance; recognized revenue may be materially lower.
FY26 included $638.8 million of non-cash impairments primarily tied to decommissioning Bitcoin mining hardware, showing material transition cost and asset-obsolescence exposure.
A delay in commissioning, testing or customer acceptance would widen the gap between contracted ARR and recognized GAAP revenue.
Financing timing can lag GPU/site commitments, increasing liquidity sensitivity during rapid expansion.
Project-level covenant or cash-flow underperformance can restrict distributions or lead to acceleration/enforcement against secured assets.
Convertible debt and future equity/equity-linked financing can dilute existing shareholders even when project funding remains available.

The 10-K states demand for NVIDIA GPUs and certain networking equipment exceeds supply and that IREN sources important AI hardware from a limited number of suppliers, creating delivery and cost sensitivity.
IREN expects substantial additional capital requirements and may commit to GPU purchases or site development before related financing or customer contracts are complete.
Microsoft Horizon 2-4 delivery grace periods extending into early Q2 2027 mean Q4 2026 target dates should not be treated as hard realized-revenue dates.

If a funded Microsoft tranche is validly terminated and a qualified replacement customer is not secured during the remarketing period, parent guarantees can expose IREN to allocated debt/note and termination-related obligations described in the filing.
Issuer governance policies establish formal controls but do not by themselves prove long-duration stewardship quality or eliminate founder/control and capital-allocation risk.
Financing and commissioning execution can delay or dilute conversion of contracted demand into per-share value.
